arguments.query: small business needs help with data analysis or reporting

results.text: A repair business has conflicting public descriptions of what its standard service includes, and customers keep asking the same questions.
A neighborhood organization says recurring volunteers struggle to understand its handoff and event setup process.
A volunteer group says its donation and attendance records are spread across several inconsistent spreadsheets.

arguments.scope: Create a single clear, consistent "Standard Service Includes" document for the repair business: one-page written summary listing exactly what is included/excluded in the standard service, common add-ons, and pricing notes if provided, plus a short FAQ addressing the top 5 recurring customer questions. Delivered as plain text ready to post on website/social/printed handout.

arguments.artifact: {"brief_id":"dad2592bd5f67651","customer_summary":"We evaluated three proposed process changes using the scoring rule (2 × value points) − cost points − risk points, which balances expected benefit against implementation cost and risk. Process Change 1 scores highest (119) because its very high value (95) outweighs its moderate cost and risk. Process Change 3 is a strong, lower-risk alternative (118), essentially tied, with zero risk points. Process Change 2 scores much lower (63) due to lower value relative to its cost and risk.
